The split of 72 people (Human-AI) to 136 (Human-Human) is about 1:2. It fits the power-analysis target of 'a minimum sample size of 65 pairs per group', with one person per Human-AI pair and two per Human-Human pair. summary: The PDF states that participants were randomly assigned to a prompt-engineered GPT-4o partner (72 pairs) or a human partner (68 pairs) (p. 1, Abstract; p. 4, Methods) and that the turn role was randomized too (p. 4), which supports the form's assignment, arms, and ai_tool coding, including the between-subjects structure, the other_aid human-partner arm, and the 72 and 136 people counts. Two gaps leave criterion 1 intact: the paper does not describe its allocation mechanism (the 1:2 split of people fits its target of equal pairs per group), and the pair-level scores include GPT-4o's own responses while the Human-Only models score only the participants' own work.
